description.narrative: The project concerns an investment in a reforestation project with a total size of 10,000 to 20,000 hectares in the coastal zone of Kenya.The aim is to restore degraded forest areas into productive, ecologically and socially functioning landscapes. The total project will require an estimated investment of EUR 25-35 million (blended financing), which will be invested in phases (first phase EUR 4-5 million).Treevive links the project to the CO2 markets. Treevive itself invests at an early stage and is committed to attract larger investors and companies (carbon credit buyers). Treevive supports the setting up of an operating company that ensure the implementation and management of the project.Extended version:Treevive B.V. is developing sustainable forestry projects (nature based solutions) in the tropics and is offering long-term support for this project. The aim is to restore degraded forest areas into productive, ecologically and socially functioning landscapes. Treevive links these projects to the CO2 markets. Treevive itself invests at an early stage and is committed to attract larger investors and companies (carbon credit buyers). Treevive supports the setting up of operating companies that ensure the implementation and management of the projects.The project concerns an investment in a reforestation project with a total size of 10,000 to 20,000 hectares in the coastal zone of Kenya, which will be reforested according to three different strategies (Commercial, Conservation, Community): commercial timber plantations with different local tree species, nature restoration, and reforestation together with local communities (agro-forestry). Also for this project, Treevive will establish a local operating company together with a local company whose owner owns a farm where various reforestation models have been tested since 2019 on a smaller scale that can now be scaled up. Furthermore, land may be contributed by the local non-governmental organisation (NGO) Nature Kenya, that owns land on which natural forest vegetation can be restored. The operating company will also purchase land itself, especially for commercial timber plantations (with local tree species Melia volkensii). The business model of the project is to generate carbon credits for the international carbon market and produce high-quality wood products that also require setting up wood processing facilities. The total project will require an estimated investment of EUR 25-35 million (blended financing), which will be invested in phases (first phase EUR 4-5 million).
